title: Deployment signal briefing and preflight asks
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures the discussion from the Release Engineering weekly: deployment signal briefing, preflight checks we want enforced for the next three release trains, and an explicit list of hotfix / rollback criteria to make triage faster during the 24–72h post-deploy window. Treat as a short-term working notes + checklist; aim to convert to the runbook once we validate the thresholds during two consecutive canaries.

Meeting info:
- Date: 2025-01-22
- Time: 09:00 PT
- Attendees: Aisha (release eng lead), Marcus (serving runtime), Lea (SRE), Omar (console/observability), Priya (platform infra), Kate (oncall rotation, joined briefly)
- Slack thread: #release-triage (pinned messages: deploy-packages-2025-01-22)

Agenda (30m):
1) Quick state: last rollout (2025-01-16) anomalies and follow-ups (5m)
2) Define deployment signal set for Q1 release trains (15m)
3) Preflight checklist additions and owners (5m)
4) Hotfix and rollback criteria + quick action routing (5m)

Notes / Discussion:
1) Previous rollout summary:
- Background: 2025-01-16 rollout of runtime v2.9.1 with optimized KV cache path. Observed a transient 12–18% regression in tail latency for 95th p50 across a subset of low-memory hosts; autoscaler responded but some routes saw increased errors (502) for ~12 minutes.
- Root cause (investigating): regressions traced to an early eviction race in the new cache admission path on GPU machines with >24 concurrent sessions. PR #4089 reverted early but left the opt-in flag.
- Lessons: need a canary profile that includes high-concurrency short-seq workloads (chat bursts) not just steady-state throughput.

2) Proposed deployment signal set (signals we will check within first 30m and 3h):
- Infra health signals (owner: Priya):
  - Node heartbeats and kube node readiness (no >2% nodes flapping)
  - GPU memory OOM events (zero tolerated in canary)
- Runtime performance (owner: Marcus):
  - 99th token latency delta vs baseline (fail if >25% increase for >5m)
  - Token failure rate (generation errors per 1k tokens) (fail if >3x baseline or >2.0 errors/1k)
  - KV cache hit ratio drop (fail if relative drop >15%)
- Application-level (owner: Omar):
  - Customer-facing error rate (5xx) aggregated across routes (fail if >2% absolute increase)
  - Tail user-visible latency for prioritized routes (see prioritized_routes doc) (fail if >20% increase)
- Observability/telemetry (owner: Lea):
  - Metrics ingestion lag and traces sample rate unchanged (critical false negatives if ingestion fails)
  - Alerts firing count (fail if >5 unexpected alerts in the first 30m)

3) Canary strategy updates:
- Canary window: rolling canary over 3% of traffic for 30 minutes, then 10% for 1 hour, then ramp to 50% over 2 hours if green.
- Traffic routing: route by route pins per product (console, hosted-api, embeddings). Have immediate fallback routing to previous model variant if route-level errors exceed criteria.
- Canary profiles: add a synthetic high-concurrency short-sequence profile as a background load generator during canary (owner: Marcus). This will exercise cache admission and eviction behavior.

4) Preflight checklist additions (explicit asks to be verified before authorizing release):
- Config and artifact checks (owner: Aisha): tags match release notes, signature verified, provenance linked in release ticket (JIRA-RELEASE-3412).
- Infra capacity (owner: Priya): reserve scaling headroom of 25% for first 4 hours post-deploy in each region.
- Feature flags: opt-in flags for new kernel paths must be default-off unless proven safe; flag matrix validated in staging with identical load profile.
- Observability gating (owner: Omar): dashboards populated and debug traces enabled for canary IDs; alert thresholds auto-created for new metrics.
- Rollback plan: documented rollback playbook linked and smoke tests prewritten (owner: Lea). Test rollback in staging once per release train.

5) Hotfix / rollback criteria (explicit — use these to escalate immediately):
- Immediate abort and rollback when:
  - Any single route sees sustained (>10m) user-visible 5xx >5% absolute (not relative) above baseline.
  - 99th token latency >2x baseline for prioritized routes for >15m.
  - Token failure rate >5 errors/1k tokens for >10m.
  - Any reproducible correctness/regression in model outputs tied to core API contracts (examples: function calling broken, structured output schema incompatible).
- Conditional rollback alert (investigate and possibly rollback):
  - API error increase between 1.5x–5x baseline for >20m (context: if mitigation available — e.g., autoscaler or model throttle — consider soften ramp)
  - Infrastructure flapping affecting >3 nodes in a cluster within 30m.
6) Triage and routing for hotfixes:
- First 5 minutes: oncall posts summary in #release-triage with links to the canary ID and primary alerts; pager duty to release-eng lead if criteria met.
- 5–30 minutes: triage call (implicit warroom) with release-eng + SRE + runtime eng + observability. Document hypothesis in the JIRA ticket and append telem snapshots.
- 30–90 minutes: attempt mitigation (route-level fallback, disable new kernel path, throttle traffic). If mitigation fails to materially improve signals in 30 minutes, trigger rollback.

7) Quick action items assigned (owners + eta):
- Marcus: deploy canary high-concurrency generator to canary cluster and add synthetic traffic profile (ETA: 2025-01-27).
- Priya: adjust autoscaler headroom policy template for release periods (ETA: 2025-01-24).
- Omar: create one-click dashboard for the deployment signal set with runbook links (ETA: 2025-01-25).
- Lea: update rollback runbook with step-by-step validation smoke test checklist and add to linked_artifacts (ETA: 2025-01-26).
- Aisha: finalize the release checklist and gate matrix, post in #release-notices, and schedule dry-run for next release train (ETA: 2025-01-28).

Open questions / unresolved:
- Should we expand canary to 5% by default for model-sensitive routes? (action: product to weigh in by 2025-01-24)
- Do we want automated rollback for token-failure-rate anomalies? (safety risk: auto rollback could trigger oscillations; action: propose threshold and cooldown to eng-safety by 2025-01-30)

Appendix (quick links & references):
- Prioritized routes doc: confluence:prioritized-routes-2025-q1
- Rollback playbook (working copy): confluence:rollback-playbook-v2
- PRs referenced: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4089, https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123
- Postmortem for 2025-01-16 incident (internal): JIRA-INC-1299

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this lightweight — team prefers short bulleted lists vs long prose. We'll iterate after next canary.
- If we see repeated false positives on KV cache drop, adjust threshold to relative drop >25% and rely on debug logs for root cause rather than rolling back immediately.

---
Revision history:
- 2025-01-21: initial draft by Aisha
- 2025-01-22: meeting notes + action items added
- 2025-01-23: clarified canary windows and added owners for signals
